info.bio:
Weezer es una banda de rock alternativo procedente de Los Angeles, Estados Unidos, y liderada por Rivers Cuomo. Se formaron el Día de San Valentín de 1992 y hasta la fecha han publicado 7 álbumes de estudio, han vendido 8 millones de discos en EE.UU.

El grupo se formó el 14 de febrero de 1992 en Los Ángeles, por Rivers Cuomo (voz y guitarra), Matt Sharp (bajo), Patrick Wilson (batería) y Jason Cropper (guitarra). A las cinco semanas dieron su primer concierto, teloneando a Dogstar, la banda del actor Keanu Reeves.

scenes.name: Hardcore en la era del punk-pop: emocore, ska-core y post-hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Mientras las revistas anuncian la «muerte del punk», el hardcore se convierte en un movimiento que no deja pueblo sin tocar y genera subgéneros. El «emocore» (Jawbreaker, Weezer, Sunny Day Real Estate, Promise Ring, At The Drive-In, Jimmy Eat World, Seaweed); el hardcore progresivo de Washington (Nation Of Ulysses, Make-Up, Shudder To Think, Jawbox, Edsel, Lungfish, Circus Lupus, Dismemberment Plan); el «ska-core» (Operation Ivy, Rancid, Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Sublime, No Doubt); el punk-pop que llega a las listas (Green Day, Offspring, Flop, Pennywise, Pegboy, Superchunk, Queers); el garage-punk californiano (Drive Like Jehu, Rocket From The Crypt, Blink 182, Zen Guerrilla); el jazzcore (Bazooka, Iceburn); la vieja escuela (D Generation, Supersuckers, Zeke, Dropkick Murphys, Silverfish, Turbonegro) y el post-hardcore de Unwound.

podcast.title: Goat Punishment Secret Shows (November 1998)
podcast.body: In November 1998, Weezer played a secret show in Hollywood under the name Goat Punishment, during which they performed six Nirvana songs, including "Swapmate" from *Bleach* and "Aneurysm," the B-side of "Smells Like Teen Spirit." A second Goat Punishment show days later featured Oasis covers. "In November 1998, Weezer played a secret show in Hollywood under the name Goat Punishment, during which they played Swapmate, which is deep on Nirvana's Bleach Amble, and Aneurysm, which you'll find is the B-side of Snows like Teen Spirit."

podcast.body: Rumors sprouted that Rivers Cuomo was in rehearsal with Nirvana for a full reunion, with Kurt Cobain, at Coachella sometime around the year 2000. "It did not, however, stop rumors from sprouting that Rivers was in rehearsal with Nirvana for a reunion, a full Nirvana reunion with Kurt, I guess, at Coachella sometime around 2000."

podcast.title: Return from Hiatus (2000)
podcast.body: Weezer participated in the Warped Tour in 2000, which served as their method for easing back into performing after a hiatus. This break occurred between their _Pinkerton_ album in 1996 and the _Green Album_ in 2001, during which Rivers Cuomo attended Harvard. "Warped was their way of easing themselves back into the game after Rivers Cuomo took time to go to Harvard."

podcast.body: Weezer initially seemed to miss the growing Twitter campaign started by Mary Klym for them to cover Toto's "Africa." The only direct response came from drummer Patrick Wilson, who simply tweeted "I laughed." "Otherwise, none of the crickets."

podcast.body: The music video for "Pork and Beans" featured appearances by prominent internet personalities of the day, including the "dramatic chipmunk," the "leave Brittany alone guy," and Tay Zonday (singer of "Chocolate Rain"). This was a clever and timely way to capture the online zeitgeist. "It featured appearances by the biggest internet stars of the day, ranging from the dramatic chipmunk to the leave Brittany alone guy to Taze On Day, the singer of Chocolate Rain."

podcast.body: The release of "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" was promoted with an extensive campaign involving 24 videos posted on YouTube. This demonstrated a heavy reliance on digital platforms for album marketing. "This release was promoted with 24 videos on YouTube."

podcast.title: 25th Anniversary and Cover Song Reputation
podcast.body: Weezer celebrated their 25th anniversary and had developed a reputation for playfully covering other artists' material during their tours, including songs by Lady Gaga, Blur, Nirvana, Pink Floyd, Black Sabbath, The Clash, Green Day, The Beach Boys, and Coldplay. "Weezer had just celebrated their 25th anniversary."

podcast.title: Archetypical Nerd Rock Band
podcast.body: Weezer is considered the ultimate nerd rock band, characterized by the quirky and bookish personality of its leader, Rivers Cuomo, who is described as neurotic and socially awkward. Their platinum records towards the end of the 1990s helped solidify the genre's presence and inspire more nerd rock bands. "We talked about them as the archetypical nerd rock band off the top of the show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Nerd Rock

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Allergy and Chocolate Preferences
podcast.body: The rider included a strict prohibition against shellfish and peanuts, citing the risk of band members going into anaphylactic shock. Weezer also expressed a fondness for European chocolate bars, which had to contain at least 55% cocoa, with 70% cocoa content being preferred. "No shellfish, no peanuts. Apparently there are some who may risk going into anaphylactic shock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Backstage Rider

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Environmental and Relaxation Requirements
podcast.body: The band's rider stipulated "no styrofoam anywhere" backstage. Additionally, it required a quiet room to be set aside backstage specifically for meditation, highlighting a focus on environmental consciousness and mental well-being. "Oh, and a quiet room needs to be set aside backstage for meditation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Backstage Rider

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Strict Dietary Restrictions
podcast.body: Weezer's rider emphasized vegetarian and organic food only, suggesting soup or vegetarian chili as good options. They specifically requested a particular type of sprouted whole grain bread and explicitly warned against providing blueberry or black raspberry jam, stating a preference for strawberry. "It's just best to stick with strawberry for Weiser."

podcast.title: Band Members' Side Projects & Acting
podcast.body: During Weezer's hiatus after "Make Believe," drummer Patrick Wilson and bassist Scott Shriner worked on a group called The Relationship. Brian Bell pursued his side project, The Special Goodness. Pat and Brian also ventured into acting in a film called "Factory Girl," with Pat playing John Cale of The Velvet Underground and Brian portraying Andy Warhol. "drummer Patrick Wilson and bass player Scott Schreiner went to work on a group called The Relationship."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Band Name Suggestions
podcast.body: Before settling on Weezer, the band considered several unconventional names including "60 wrong sausages," "Fuzz," "Bush" (not the famous one), "Goat Punishment," "Outhouse," "Hummingbird," and "the big Jones." They even recorded a four-track demo as "60 wrong sausages" called "The Colustraal EP." "One of the names they considered was 60 wrong sausages."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Band's Collective Songwriting on Red Album
podcast.body: For the Red Album, Pat Wilson, Brian Bell, and Scott Shriner also contributed songs, marking a more collaborative songwriting effort beyond Rivers Cuomo's primary role. Scott Shriner described his musical contributions as "just based on feeling," with Rivers often writing the lyrics. "Pat Brian and Scott wrote songs in this album too, so I can't speak for them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Black Album Delay
podcast.body: The Black Album was initially planned to follow the White Album, intended to be a darker counterpart. However, the songs Rivers Cuomo developed were not dark enough, leading to the Black Album being put on hold. What was released instead was Pacific Daydream. "So they had no choice but to put the Black Album on hold."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Black Hole Sessions Repurposing
podcast.body: Although *Songs from the Black Hole* was never officially released, many recordings from these sessions were repurposed for other albums, released in different forms, or appeared on Rivers Cuomo's solo recordings *Alone, the Home Recordings of Rivers Cuomo* (Volumes 1 and 2). "However, there were plenty of recordings floating about from the Black Hole sessions. Some of the songs were repurposed or released in other forms and other albums, and Rivers released a bunch of this material on two volumes of solo recordings called Alone, the Home Recordings of Rivers Cuomo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bus Accident on Ratitude Tour
podcast.body: On December 6, 2009, while on tour for the "Ratitude" album, Weezer's bus hit a patch of ice on the New York State Thruway near Glen. The bus went over the median, hit posts, crossed the highway again, jumped a guard rail, and landed in a ditch. Rivers Cuomo, his wife Kyoko, daughter Mia, nanny, and assistant Sarah were on board. Rivers sustained three cracked ribs and internal bleeding, leading to the cancellation of the remaining tour dates. "On December 6th, 2009, Weezer was on tour for the Ratitude album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Spike Jonze
podcast.body: Spike Jonze, whose background in skate videos influenced the fluid and amateur aesthetic of his videoclips, worked with Weezer. "Ha trabajado con Rem, Sonic Jews, Darth Punk, Wither, Bjork, Ockini West, y también ha dado su salto al cine con obras como Ser John Balcomico."

podcast.title: Computer Program for Teal Album Covers Selection
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo wrote a computer program that analyzed Spotify data to select songs for the Teal Album. The program identified popular songs not tagged as Alt Rock or Classic Rock and narrowed the list to those released before 1994, generating 200 titles for the band to consider. "Rivers wrote a computer program that sucked in all kinds of Spotify data."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Consistent Geekiness
podcast.body: Weezer has consistently celebrated their geekiness without reservation, both in their song lyrics and their music videos, making them a quintessential example of Geek Rock. "They've continued to celebrate their geekiness with no reservations whatsoever in both their songs and their music videos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 7: The Other Genres

podcast.title: Demos Widely Shared
podcast.body: As early as 2005, Weezer was sharing demos widely with fans through their website, which was a novel approach at the time. This practice demonstrated their commitment to transparency and involving their fanbase, as exemplified by a slightly different mix demo of "Beverly Hills" from "Make Believe." "Demos like that were widely shared by Weezer with fans through their website, something that was pretty novel for 2005."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Early Rehearsal Conditions
podcast.body: After moving into a house at 2226 Amherst Avenue in Los Angeles, the band spent hours rehearsing in the garage under stark conditions, including no refrigerator and only outdoor lawn furniture for seating indoors, reflecting their poverty at the time. "There was no refrigerator. And the only thing they had to sit on inside was outside lawn furniture."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Everything Will Be All Right in the End Cassette Release
podcast.body: Weezer released "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" on cassette, making them one of the few bands to anticipate the eventual resurgence of cassettes as collectibles for hardcore fans. This demonstrates a forward-thinking approach to niche physical formats. "Weezer released a version on Kasek, making them one of the very few bands to predict that Kasek would eventually become kind of a thing again, at least when it comes to collectibles in the world of hardcore fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Extensive Demos and Unreleased Material
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo has an immense catalog of demos, possibly thousands, some dating back as far as 1979, which he has posted online or released on compilations. This extensive archive provides numerous "rabbit holes" for fans to explore. "There are hundreds, well, probably thousands, literally thousands, of demos that Rivers Cuomo has either posted online or released on compilations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Extensive Influences
podcast.body: Weezer's influences are broad and deep within the Powerpop lineage, including foundational bands like The Beatles, The Ramones, Cheap Trick, The Knack, and The Cars, as well as The Pixies. This wide array of influences supports the argument that they are currently the leading Powerpop band in the world. "Their influences include the Beatles, the Ramones, Cheap Trick, the Nack, the Cars, the Pixies, ensure just about every single band that we've mentioned so far."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Power Pop

podcast.title: External Collaborators and Multiple Producers for Ratitude
podcast.body: For "Ratitude," Weezer brought in outside collaborators for the first time, including Jermaine Dupri, members of All-American Rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan (though uncredited and parts recorded in 2003). The album also had four producers, including Dr. Luke and Jacknife Lee, plus Rivers Cuomo, totaling five. "For the first time outside collaborators were brought in, including Germain Dupree, a couple of guys from all American rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Fan Collaboration for "Turning Up the Radio"
podcast.body: The project "Let's Write a Song" (SAWNG) for the track "Turning Up the Radio" involved fans submitting ideas for song titles, chord progressions, lyrics, and melodies through YouTube videos. This highly creative and interactive project utilized the ideas of 16 different fans, alongside Rivers Cuomo's contributions, for the final song on "Death to False Metal." "The project was called Let's Write a Song, and song is spelled S-A-W-N-G in this particular case."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Fan Engagement through Official Website
podcast.body: Weezer maintains a "very well-developed and sophisticated fan club" and actively provides fans with unique material not found on their commercial CDs via their official website. This demonstrates the band's "generosity with their fans" in sharing raw demo recordings. "Weezer gets this. They not only have a very well-developed and sophisticated fan club, but they also feed fans with cool material that's not on any of their CDs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Tracking Down Demos

podcast.title: Fan Focus Groups for Everything Will Be All Right in the End
podcast.body: Weezer involved their fans directly in the creation of "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" by holding focus groups. Fans listened to demos and songs still in progress, and their feedback was incorporated into the final product. This level of fan involvement was unusual for a band. "The band once again turned to their fans, holding focus groups to listen to demos and songs that were still works in progress."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: First Gig and Band Naming
podcast.body: The band's first offer to play came on March 19, 1992, at a club called Rodgies, headlining Dog Star, which featured Keanu Reeves on bass. Needing a proper permanent name for the gig, Rivers Cuomo, Patrick Wilson, Jason Cropper, and Matt Sharp chose "Weezer," a nickname Rivers had been given by his father, referencing a character in "The Little Rascals." "And eventually Rivers, Pat, Jason, and bass player Matt Sharp now went with the name Weezer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Formula for Success
podcast.body: Weezer has perfected a formula that has worked for decades, combining musical talent, wit, self-deprecation, left-of-center thinking, a desire for fun, a willingness to experiment, clever marketing, and, crucially, an open approach with their fans. This inclusive strategy has been key to their longevity. "They have perfected a formula that includes musical talent, wit, self-deprecation, left of center thinking, a desire to have fun, a willingness to experiment, some very clever marketing, and above all, to let their fans in on everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Four-Year Break Before Everything Will Be All Right in the End
podcast.body: Weezer took a significant four-year break from releasing "proper records" between "Hurley" (September 2010) and "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" (October 2014). This was their longest hiatus between studio albums in a while. "Weezer took a four-year break from making proper records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Harvard Enrollment Impact
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo's enrollment at Harvard in the fall of 1995 contributed to the abandonment of the *Songs from the Black Hole* project, as he "didn't really have any time for this rock and roll silliness anymore." "Rivers had enrolled at Harvard and didn't really have any time for this rock and roll silliness anymore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Lost Albums

podcast.title: Inspired by Ian Curtis's Lyrics
podcast.body: American band Weezer has been greatly inspired by Ian Curtis's lyrical style. "En Estados Unidos tenemos bandas como Wills, que se han inspirado mucho sobre todo en las letras y en Cortes."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Especial JOY DIVISION: 4. La banda tras el final

podcast.title: Jason Cropper's Departure from Blue Album Sessions
podcast.body: Guitarist Jason Cropper left the group during the recording sessions for "The Blue Album" due to "legal issues" surrounding his departure. One story suggests he was asked to leave because his girlfriend was pregnant, and he wasn't handling it well, raising concerns about his commitment to the band. Brian Bell, an early fan, was invited to replace him. "Guitarist Jason Cropper left the group during the recording sessions. And it's unclear what happened because there are, well, legal issues surrounding his departure."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Journal and Spreadsheet for Lyrics
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo stored vocal thoughts in a journal, selecting the best bits to transfer to a spreadsheet. This spreadsheet was organized by the number of syllables in each line and by "strong weak emphasis," a concept likely learned from his English degree. He then ordered the data to fit melodies and tell stories. "Vocal thoughts were stored in a journal with the best bits making it onto a spreadsheet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Leaked Tracks Forcing Album Release
podcast.body: Eight tracks from the real "Deliverance Is At Hand" album were leaked online, which compelled the record label to accelerate the album's release date. This demonstrates the impact of early online leaks on album rollout strategies. "Eight tracks from the album, the real album, or leaked, which actually forced the label's hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Longevity and Stability
podcast.body: Weezer has been together for more than 30 years, notably without any breakups, reunions, or official hiatuses, showcasing unusual stability for a rock band. "Weezer has been together for more than 30 years. There have been no breakups and no reunions."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Lyric and Tempo Evolution
podcast.body: "Buddy Holly" underwent several changes during its production. Early demos contained rap slang that was later removed. The lyrics initially referred to Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire but eventually morphed into Mary Tyler Moore and Buddy Holly. Furthermore, the song's tempo was increased in the studio and further tweaked to a higher pace during the mastering process. "Instead of the lyrics referring to Ginger Rogers and Fred Astaire, they morphed into Mary Tyler Moore and Buddy Holly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Mary Kinchen's Africa Cover Request
podcast.body: The band's cover of Toto's "Africa" originated from a persistent request, described as a "demand," from a 14-year-old fan in Cleveland named Mary Kinchen, who tweeted at Weezer. Her tweet, "it's about time you blessed the reins down in Africa," prompted the band to first cover Toto's "Rosanna" before eventually recording "Africa." "It grew out of a request, well, actually more of a demand. From a 14-year-old fan in Cleveland named Mary Kim, she tweeted at the band, it's about time you blessed the reins down in Africa."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Mickey and Carly Allen Car Accident
podcast.body: Following their tour for "Pinkerton" through late 1996 to mid-1997, Weezer postponed everything after early fans Mickey and Carly Allen, who ran the official fan club, died in a car accident with their sister Trista while driving home from a Weezer show in Denver. After mourning, the band decided to take a three-year break. "Everything had to be postponed, though, when Mickey and Carly Allen, two early fans who ran the official Weaser fan club, died in a car accident with their sister Trista."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Miscategorization as Emo
podcast.body: Weezer was sometimes incorrectly associated with the Emo scene during its peak popularity, despite not being an Emo band. This reflects how various alt-rock bands were broadly categorized into prevailing trends, sometimes inaccurately. "Even bands that weren't Emo, like Green Day and Weezer, believe it or not, were wrongly lumped into this scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Nerd Rock Persona
podcast.body: Weezer is considered the "ultimate nerd rock band of all time," largely due to the quirky, bookish, neurotic, and socially awkward personality of its leader, Rivers Cuomo, combined with the often self-referential and meme-laden content of their music videos. "we have a primo nerd rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Nerd Rock

podcast.title: Non-Conflicting Schedules with Nirvana
podcast.body: A theory points out that there has never been any recording studio bookings or tour dates that conflicted between Weezer and Nirvana, suggesting that if one band was on the road, the other was in the studio, and vice-versa. "There never has been any recording studio bookings or tour dates that conflicted with either band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

podcast.title: Numerous Collaborations and Writing Credits
podcast.body: Weezer, or its members, have engaged in a large number of collaborations, guest appearances, and writing credits with various artists. These include A.W. Nation, Billy Talent, Todd Rundgren, Panic! at the Disco, and even The Muppets, with approximately three dozen such collaborative songs identified. "There are all the guest appearances and writing credits unrecorded by A.W. Nation, Billy Talent, Todd Rungren, Panic of the Disco, and even The Muppets."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Online Clues and Disinformation for Deliverance Is At Hand
podcast.body: Prior to the release of "Deliverance Is At Hand," several online clues emerged, including a leaked and deleted demo called "Pig" (metadata revealed its origin). A mysterious website, "Album 6," not affiliated with Weezer, also appeared, promoting a fake album ("Toot En Song") but ultimately directing fans to the official Weezer site. The "Weezer Zone" was flooded with fake news, rumors, leaks, and bogus lyrics, creating widespread disinformation. "But then some clues started appearing online. A demo called Pig was leaked and then deleted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Personal Tragedies and Birth of Son Leo
podcast.body: After the bus accident, Rivers Cuomo experienced further personal challenges, including the death of former bassist Mikey Welsh from an overdose in a Chicago hotel room on October 8, 2011. He also lost his grandfather, a former girlfriend, and his meditation teacher. In 2012, Rivers and Kyoko had a son, Leo, whose birth was difficult. These events prompted Rivers to seek a slower pace after a period of prolific releases. "On October 8th, 2011, former bass player Mikey Welsh was found dead of an overdose in a Chicago hotel room."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Plugged into Memes
podcast.body: The band Weezer is notably "very plugged into memes," a characteristic that contributed to their eventual engagement with the "Africa" cover campaign, which gained traction partly due to the song's meme status. "And if there's one thing Weezer is, it's that they're very plugged into memes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 9 Great Alt-Rock Cover Songs

podcast.title: Post-Make Believe Breakup Rumors
podcast.body: After the "Make Believe" album cycle, rumors circulated that Weezer was breaking up. This was fueled by Rivers Cuomo returning to Harvard, his marriage, and other band members focusing on side projects, along with Rivers' own quote in an interview suggesting the band was "done for the moment." "However, after this album cycle was completed, there were rumors that Weezer was breaking up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Producer Ric Ocasek's Persuasion
podcast.body: Despite Rivers Cuomo's strong reservations, producer Ric Ocasek, leader of The Cars, was adamant about including "Buddy Holly" on the debut album. He, along with the other band members, insisted on its inclusion. Ocasek eventually convinced Cuomo by suggesting they record it, and if Cuomo still disliked it, they could leave it off, but warning him it would be "stupid not to include it." "But Rico Kasek, the leader of the cars and the guy tapped to produce the record, would have none of that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Producer Selection for Debut Album
podcast.body: When asked by Geffen Records who they wanted to produce their debut, Weezer initially boldly suggested they would do it themselves. When pushed for names, someone jokingly suggested Ric Ocasek of The Cars, not expecting it to happen, but Ocasek turned out to be interested. They recorded a practice demo with him on August 11, 1993, and got along great. "Someone in Weezer said, you know, we really like the cars. Get us Ricokasic. That was meant as a joke."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Programmers for Pacific Daydream Spreadsheet
podcast.body: For the Pacific Daydream album, Rivers Cuomo hired programmers to organize his songwriting data in an even more granular way. They tagged everything with specific attributes, and one tab in his spreadsheet contained about 5,500 "cool" lyrical fragments, which he used when stuck for inspiration. The programmers used Python for this task. "During this time, he hired some programmers to organize the data in an even more granular way, tagging everything with specific attributes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Prolific Output and "Too Much Weezer" Criticism
podcast.body: Weezer has maintained a "furious pace" of releasing new material, leading some critics and fans to suggest they are "too prolific" and that the sheer volume of music might dilute its impact. Despite this, the band continues to move ahead with new projects. "In fact, some people say that they're maybe a little too prolific."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Prolific Period After Red Album
podcast.body: The Red Album marked the beginning of a highly prolific period for Weezer, with another album, "Ratitude," released little more than a year later. This suggested an increased creative output from the band. "The red album marked the beginning of a very prolific period for the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Quirky and Eccentric Band Type
podcast.body: Weezer exemplifies the "quirky, eccentric, and weird" type of band that makes music fun and unpredictable. They balance this with widespread appeal, possessing "just enough of the nerd factor" to stand out without alienating audiences. This requires songwriting skills, careful image management, and creativity. "And among the very, very, very, very best of this class is Weezer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Red Album Liner Notes
podcast.body: The host was surprised to find his interview with the band incorporated into the liner notes of his CD copy of the Red Album. This was an unusual and unexpected inclusion. "Now imagine my surprise when I opened my copy, my CD copy, and saw that my interview with the band had been incorporated into the liner notes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Return of Bigger Older Acts Post 9/11
podcast.body: Weezer was among the bigger, older acts that saw a renewed wave of popularity after the events of 9/11 and the subsequent military conflicts, playing a role in the renewed interest in rock music during the mid-2000s. "And a return of some bigger older acts, U2, 9-H nails, Green Day, Weezer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

podcast.title: Ric Ocasek's Guitar Preference
podcast.body: During the production of "Everything Will Be All Right in the End," Ric Ocasek insisted that the band use the same guitars they had on the "Blue Album." This was part of his effort to bring Weezer's sound back to their early days. "Rico Kasek insisted on using the same guitars as the band had on the blue record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Ric Ocasek's Production and Return to Early Sound
podcast.body: Ric Ocasek of The Cars produced "Everything Will Be All Right in the End," making it his third and final album with Weezer before his death, having previously produced the Blue and Green Albums. Ocasek was specifically hired to guide Weezer back to their earlier sound. "This was the third and last album to be produced by Rico Cacic of the Cars before he died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rise of New Alternative Bands (Mid-90s)
podcast.body: Weezer was one of the new bands emerging in the mid-1990s as alternative music gained widespread acceptance. "We had new bands like Weezer and Rage Against the Machine and Beck and the Cranberries in the Verve."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 500th Show!

podcast.title: Ritalin and Tequila Songwriting Experiments
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo's creative process for some songs, including "Hashpipe" and "Dope Nose," involved unusual experiments he called his "catalog of riffs." These entailed plugging in a guitar, taking one Ritalin pill with three shots of tequila, going into the backyard, and sometimes closing his eyes to see if songs appeared in his mind. "The creation of a lot of this material involved plugging in a guitar, taking one riddle in pill with three shots of tequila and then going out into the backyard to see what happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Riverpedia / The Library / Drive Times App
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo created something called the "Riverpedia," now known as "The Library," which began as a homework assignment and was posted online on August 18, 2020. This evolved into an app called "Drive Times," designed to automate tour logistics like scheduling venue arrivals, road travel, and private plane flights. He learned to code in Python during the pandemic lockdown to create this. "He created something called the Riverpedia, which is now known as the Library."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Coding Skills
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo dedicated part of the pandemic lockdown to learning to code himself, ultimately creating the "Drive Times" app for tour logistics. He achieved a 95 in his coding class and is described as a "pretty fair Python programmer." "In case you're wondering, Rivers got a 95 in his coding class."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Experimental Approach to Ratitude
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo embraced an experimental mindset for "Ratitude," telling the band, "this is just one more album out of many more that we're going to make." This indicated a willingness to take risks, suggesting that if an experiment didn't work out, they would simply try something different for the next album. "So in other words, if it works out great, if it doesn't, fine, we'll do something different for the next album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Friendship with King He
podcast.body: The song "Buddy Holly" was a direct result of Rivers Cuomo's protectiveness over his Korean friend, King He. Cuomo became "really pissed off" when other band members made fun of her, recalling how she was often picked on in high school. The song was written as an expression of his commitment to their platonic relationship and his readiness to defend her. "It's about a particular girl I knew."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Home Recordings
podcast.body: A number of other songs from the aborted *Songs from the Black Hole* project appear on Rivers Cuomo's Home Recordings releases. "If you want to go deeper into this aborted record, a number of other songs from Songs from the Black Hole appear on Rivers Home Recordings releases."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Concept Albums: Part 1

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Initial Rejection of "Buddy Holly"
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo initially refused to consider including "Buddy Holly" on Weezer's debut album, deeming it "too cheesy" and an outlier compared to his other compositions. He felt it didn't fit the band's intended sound. "For the longest time, he refused to consider including the song and Weezer's debut album because it was too cheesy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Meditation Practice (Vipassanā)
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo practices Vipassanā meditation, a Sanskrit term meaning "to see things as they are," which has been around for at least 2,500 years. He practices at least two hours a day. Producer Rick Rubin first suggested it around 2003 when Weezer was working on the Red Album. Rivers initially feared it would rob him of angst but found it enhanced his creativity and made him "10% happier." "It's called Vispasana, that's Sanskrit for to see things as they are."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Metal Band Past
podcast.body: The album "Van Weezer" was noted as a return to Rivers Cuomo's musical roots, specifically referencing his past in a metal band before forming Weezer. This informed the heavier sound of the album. "Remember how Rivers was in a metal band before Weezer? This was a return to that time, sort of."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Personal Life & Hiatus
podcast.body: Following the "Make Believe" album, Rivers Cuomo returned to Harvard to finish his English degree. He married Kyoko Ito on June 18, 2006, after meeting her in 1997, with a ceremony on a remote beach near Malibu and a honeymoon in Japan. During this period, he made a comment during his honeymoon interview suggesting the band might be "done," which contributed to breakup fears when no new album appeared in 2006 or 2007. "Rivers returned to Harvard to finish his degree in English. He got married to Kyoto, Ito on June 18, 2006."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Pizza Crust Habit
podcast.body: During the band's early, poor days, Rivers Cuomo would save pizza crusts in a fanny pack to eat later, demonstrating the band's financial struggles. "They were so poor that Rivers would save pizza crusts in a fanny pack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Songwriting Inspiration
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo primarily draws inspiration from his own life and feelings, starting with personal experiences and then using "a little artistry" to make the songs more relatable. He confirmed that his songs for this particular album came directly from his life, though he couldn't speak for other band members' contributions. "My favorite source of inspiration is my own life and my own feelings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Rivers Cuomo's Stream of Consciousness Songwriting
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo generates a vast number of songs by embracing a "stream of consciousness" approach, letting ideas flow freely. While most of these ideas might be discarded, he believes some "gems" will emerge, contributing to his prolific output (e.g., sorting through 250 songs for the White Album, only one making the cut). "Well Rivers says he's all about stream of consciousness. He just lets the ideas flow."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Road-Testing New Material
podcast.body: During their 2000 Warped Tour performance, Weezer gave fans the opportunity to hear them road-test upcoming songs. "Warped fans would have had a chance to hear Weezer road tests upcoming songs like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 24 Years of the Warped Tour

podcast.title: Screamo Band Dispreference
podcast.body: Weezer's music was implicitly contrasted with the preferences of Screamo bands, who favored "old Joy Division and Smith records" over Weezer, indicating a different artistic sensibility and perhaps a less intense, more pop-oriented sound in comparison. "They preferred old Joy Division and Smith records over Weezer and Fugazi."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00s Part 4: Variety Returns

podcast.title: Shared Biographer with Nirvana
podcast.body: Weezer shares a biographer, John D. Luerssen, with Nirvana. Luerssen has also written books about The Smiths, Bruce Springsteen, and U2. "Nirvana and Weezer share a biographer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

podcast.title: Shared Record Label with Nirvana
podcast.body: Weezer was signed to the same record label as Nirvana. "It's true that they were signed to the same label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

podcast.title: Signature Style
podcast.body: Weezer specializes in short, quirky pop songs that often feature sharp guitars, pointed lyrics, and occasional satire. This distinctive approach firmly places them within the Powerpop genre. "They specialize in short quirky pop songs, often with sharp guitars and pointed lyrics mixed with the occasional bit of satire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Power Pop

podcast.title: Songwriting Process on Santa Monica College Campus
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo developed the lyrics for "Buddy Holly" while walking through the campus of Santa Monica College, where both he and King He were attending school. The iconic line "weew, I look just like Buddy Holly" was conceived at the same speed as his walking pace, indicating an organic, real-time inspiration. "He came up with the lyrics while walking through the campus of Santa Monica College where he and King He were attending school."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Spotify Playlists for Chord Progressions
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo developed a unique songwriting process that began with creating Spotify playlists. These playlists featured songs with chord progressions he found interesting, providing a foundation for new melodies. "Rivers began by creating Spotify playlists featuring songs with chord progression that he found interesting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Studio Dynamics and "Buddy Holly" Notes
podcast.body: During the recording sessions for Weezer's debut album, notes reading "weew, what, Buddy Holly" began to appear around the studio. This suggests the other band members and producer Ric Ocasek were playfully but persistently advocating for the song's inclusion, despite Rivers Cuomo's initial reluctance. "Little notes started appearing around the studio that said, weew, what, Buddy Holly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Tagged as Emo
podcast.body: Weezer, an LA-based band, became associated with the emo label due to their nerdy and geeky image, singer Rivers Cuomo's highly confessional lyrics (expressing fear, bitterness, and confusion), big and loud guitar sounds, and notable punk rock influences. "And one LA band that got tagged with the emo label was Weezer. And you can see why. I mean, they were nerdy and they were geeky."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 3: Emo

podcast.title: Teal Album's Surprise Digital Release
podcast.body: The Teal Album was released in January 2019 as a complete surprise digital release, without any prior warning or traditional promotional rollout. This unexpected drop was a marketing tactic in itself. "It just appeared as a digital release as a surprise, and it featured nothing but covers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: The Weezer Snuggie
podcast.body: One of the band's most famous pieces of merchandise was the Weezer Snuggie, a blanket with sleeves similar to those advertised on late-night TV. The band appeared on David Letterman wearing them, and a commercial was produced, offering the Snuggie for $29.99 with a bonus copy of the "Ratitude" CD. "It was The Weezer Snuggie. You know those blankets with the sleeves that were advertised on late night TV?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Thematic Structure of Everything Will Be All Right in the End
podcast.body: The album "Everything Will Be All Right in the End" is divided into three thematic sections: "The Panopticon Artist," which explores the relationship between Weezer and their fans; "Belodona," comprising classic girl group-style songs; and "Patriarchia," songs about father figures. The "Patriarchia" theme is particularly significant as Rivers reconciled with his birth father, who left the family in 1975 and became a Pentecostal minister. "The album can be divided into three themes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Tinder Account for Songwriting Inspiration
podcast.body: For the White Album, Rivers Cuomo signed up for a Tinder account to meet people and then wrote about those experiences. Because he was living in California, these encounters often coalesced into themes related to the beach and ocean, including surfers, beach bums, and specific characters like "Harry Christmas." "Rivers signed up for a Tinder account and he met with people and then wrote about those experiences."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Touring with Saves the Day
podcast.body: Weezer toured with fellow emo band Saves the Day, along with other established artists such as Green Day and Blink-182. "Saves the Day, definitely an emo band, toured with not just fellow travelers Weezer, but also Green Day and Blink 182, and Dashboard Confessional, Open for You too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 3: Emo

podcast.title: Transition from Meditation to Crafts
podcast.body: Rivers Cuomo developed an interest in knitting after getting into meditation in the mid-2000s. This led him to also explore clay sculptures and whittling. He used to knit in bed while his wife read Sherlock Holmes mysteries, though he now states he has less time for it due to his work commitments. "Things began when he got into meditation in the mid-Auts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hobbies of Musicians

podcast.title: Unofficial Album Leak
podcast.body: In 2001, Rivers Cuomo intentionally leaked an unofficial album online. This included at least four recording sessions from rehearsals featuring 18 new songs, and about two dozen more recorded live during the Warp Tour using an eight-track mobile unit. "They were also part of an unofficial album that was intentionally leaked online by Rivers in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: Vocalizing Guitar Solos
podcast.body: As part of his songwriting process, Rivers Cuomo would first sound out guitar solos vocally. This technique allowed him to develop the melodic contours of solos before translating them to the instrument. "Guitar solos were sounded out vocally first."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Wannabeezer Producer for White Album
podcast.body: Jack Sinclair, the producer for the White Album, was a longtime Weezer fan and also fronted a tribute band called Wannabeezer. Brian Bell later noted that Sinclair understood the band's sound better than the band members themselves, bringing a unique perspective to the production. "Jack Sinclair, who a long time Weezer fan who also fronted a band called Wannabeezer. This gave him some really crazy insights as to how the band should sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Weezer Roomba Contest for OK Human
podcast.body: For the release of "OK Human," Weezer partnered with the creators of the Roomba robot vacuum for a promotional contest. Five "Weezer Roombas" (spelled with a silent W) were offered as prizes, announced through a social media campaign claiming that "nine out of ten humans have dreamed of Weezer cleaning their house." "Weezer hooked up with the people who made the Roomba Robot Vacuum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Weezer's Early Identity Struggle
podcast.body: When Weezer first started, the band members were uncertain about their musical direction, exploring genres like metal, PowerPop, and grungy sounds. They remained a "work in progress" for a significant period before the release of their 1994 debut album. "When Weezer was first starting out, the band wasn't exactly sure what they wanted to be."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Stories Behind Songs - 5

podcast.title: Yelp Profile Promotion for Black Album
podcast.body: To promote the Black Album, an official Yelp profile was created on October 9, 2018, and shared by the official Weezer Twitter account. This profile featured reviews of places with "Black" in their names, with each review containing mysterious lyrics from the upcoming album. "On October 9th, 2018, a Yelp profile appeared and was shared by the official Weezer Twitter account."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: YouTube Invasion Promotion for Hurley
podcast.body: To promote the "Hurley" album on YouTube, Weezer launched an innovative campaign called "YouTube Invasion." They challenged 15 amateur online creators to produce something interesting in 30 minutes. One example involved "Hot for Words" trying to explain the origins of "Weezer" and "Hurley." "To promote the album on YouTube, the band gave 15 amateur online creators to come up with something interesting in 30 minutes."

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

xref.title: Post-Pinkerton Isolation and Songwriting Plan
xref.body: Following the underperformance of Weezer's second album, *Pinkerton*, Rivers Cuomo withdrew from Harvard, where he was studying music. He secluded himself in a room painted entirely black and insulated the windows, intending to purge all weaknesses and dedicate himself to crafting the "perfect pop song." "When Weezer's second album, Pinkerton, didn't do as well as Rivers Quomo had hoped, he dropped out of Harvard where he had been studying music and hid in his room, which are the walls and ceilings painted black and had the windows blacked out with layers of fiberglass insulation. The plan was to purge himself of all weaknesses so we could concentrate on writing the perfect pop song."

xref.title: Weezer Producer
xref.body: Ric Ocasek of The Cars produced three Weezer albums: the Blue Album, the Green Album, and "Everything Will Be All Right in the End." He was specifically hired for the latter to guide Weezer back to their early sound. He passed away after producing "Everything Will Be All Right in the End." "This was the third and last album to be produced by Rico Cacic of the Cars before he died."

xref.title: YouTube Invasion Participant
xref.body: "Hot for Words" was one of 15 amateur online creators who participated in Weezer's "YouTube Invasion" promotion for the "Hurley" album. They attempted to explain the origins of the words "Weezer" and "Hurley" in a 30-minute video. "This is from somebody named Hot for Words."
